prior_importants.description: The chore/refactor, docs and spike headings in the code don't match the labels in the repo's issue forms. Every form-filed chore, refactor, docs or spike ticket reports a required field as missing, and intake would strip `ready` from even a fully filled ticket.

A directory-style area such as `src/cli/ and src/core/` (the form-placeholder style) yields no module and no ADR match, so a bug or chore that crosses modules or touches an ADR area gets `needsDesign: false`.

A `# comment` line inside a fenced code block is read as a heading and splits the section there. A shell comment in a reproduction or area block can make a filled field vague, or drop its paths so the design triggers don't fire.

findings.description: For chore and refactor, `Scope boundary` is marked `area: true`. Both the form and the rubric ask that field to name what the change leaves alone, so paths the ticket stays out of fire the module-boundary and ADR-area triggers.
findings.body:
> `{ heading: 'Scope boundary', area: true },`

The code treats paths in a chore or refactor ticket's `Scope boundary` as places the work lands. The form and the rubric both define that field the other way round:

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/chore-refactor.yml` says: "Where the change stops. Name what is left as it is, even if it is tempting to touch."
- `docs/tickets/chore-refactor.md` says: "naming what is left as it is" and "The boundary names the neighbour that stays put."

`Files in scope` is the field that says where the work lands ("Nothing outside these may change"). The code's own `Field.area` doc also says "The field names where the work lands".

**Trigger:** a refactor with `Files in scope: src/core/plan.service.ts` and `Scope boundary: Only the plan service; src/cli/plan.command.ts stays as it is.`
- `triggersFor` gets paths from both fields.
- `moduleOf` returns `core` and `cli`, so `module-boundary` fires.
- `needsDesign` comes back `true` for a refactor that stays inside one module.

If the boundary names a path under an ADR glob to mark it off limits, `adr-area` fires the same way. So the more closely a ticket follows the rubric, the more likely it gets a design it doesn't need. Decision 176 says a chore needs no design unless a trigger fires.

**Fix:** drop `area: true` from this field. `Files in scope` stays an area field, so the code still doesn't fall back to reading the whole body. No current test depends on `Scope boundary` being an area field.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5eb4df857fd15a662715ee60bd1a0a25955f096b/src/core/ticket-intake.utils.ts#L34-L38

findings.description: When the area names a file by its GitHub permalink, the extracted path starts with `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/`. That path matches no ADR glob and no module, so `adr-area` and `module-boundary` don't fire and the design gate passes when it should fail.
findings.body:
> `const paths = areaText.match(PATH) ?? [];`

Bug reporters often paste a line permalink into `Suspected area`, for example `https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/main/src/claude/tmux.ts#L40`. What the code does with it:

- `PATH` can't match at `https:`, because a colon comes before the slash. The leftmost match is `github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/main/src/claude/tmux.ts`, which stops at `#`.
- `moduleOf` sees `parts[0] === 'github.com'` and returns `undefined`.
- `globToRegExp` anchors each ADR regex with `^...$` (`src/core/glob.utils.ts:25`), so `src/claude/**` doesn't match.

**Trigger:** a bug with that permalink and `adrAreas: ['src/claude/**']` returns `triggers: []` and `needsDesign: false`. A bug in an ADR area skips design. Permalinks into two modules miss `module-boundary` the same way.

The forms invite this input:
- `bug.yml` asks for "The file, module or command you suspect" in a free textarea.
- Each form already links to files with `https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/main/...` URLs.

The round-1 directory and `./` issue has a different cause. Stripping `./` doesn't remove this prefix, but both fixes belong in the same path-normalizing step before lines 149-150.

**Fix:** the suggestion strips a `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob|tree/<ref>/` prefix. It is anchored to `github.com`, so a repo directory named `blob` or `tree` is never stripped. A branch ref that contains a slash still strips only partway.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5eb4df857fd15a662715ee60bd1a0a25955f096b/src/core/ticket-intake.utils.ts#L144-L150

findings.description: `DEPENDENCY_BOX` (`/^\s*[-*+]\s+\[[xX]\].*\bdependenc/im`) is run on the whole body, not on a dependency field; no issue form has such a checkbox. So any checked task-list line that mentions dependencies fires the trigger. Trigger: a bug whose `Reproduction` has `- [x] Reinstalled dependencies with pnpm install`, or one with `- [x] Removed the unused dependency`, returns `triggers: ['dependency']` and `needsDesign: true`, even though nothing is added. One fix is to match only the wording of a dedicated box ("Adds a dependency") inside a named section.

`sections()` ends a field at any heading of levels 1 to 6. GitHub issue forms render each field as `###`, and a textarea passes the author's Markdown through unchanged, so a subheading the author writes inside a field cuts it short. Trigger: a feature whose `Acceptance criteria` is `#### CLI
- \`pup plan add\` with no scope exits 2`. The section closes at `#### CLI`, the value is `''`, the field is reported vague, and intake removes `ready` from a complete ticket. The same split hides area paths that follow a subheading: `Suspected area: The launcher.

#### Files
- src/core/launch.service.ts
- src/claude/tmux.ts` gives area text `The launcher.`, so `module-boundary` doesn't fire. The round-1 fix for fenced code blocks doesn't cover this. One fix is to split only on headings whose normalized text is a known field name for the type, or on `Estimate`.

The test is named "imports nothing that reads a file or runs a process". It actually asserts that the module's import list is exactly `['./glob.utils.js', './types/profile.types.js']`. It does not check what `glob.utils` itself pulls in. It would also fail on a harmless new import, so a reader would wrongly assume it catches impurity. Name it for what it asserts, such as "keeps its imports to glob.utils and the profile types", and let the purity claim live in the `checkTicketIntake` JSDoc.

Each field's section is looked up twice: `sectionMap.get(normalize(field.heading))` runs in the required-field loop (line 175) and again for the area fields (line 183). `triggersFor` takes the whole `sectionMap` only to read Estimate. Collect the area values in the existing loop and pass `triggersFor` the estimate text instead. That removes the second `fields.filter` pass, the repeated lookup and the `Map` parameter.
